```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5)
```

External validation of a Cox model on the NCCTG advanced lung cancer cohort (`survival::lung`). This is a small dataset, with a high proportion of events and some missing covariate data, so it exercises the small-cohort deployment gate. Fitting was done using the three largest recruiting institutes; all other institutes form the validation set, a centre split ensuring independence from development.

Modest C, broken calibration. Although C by itself looks only mediocre, the joint posterior separates the two and gives an unambiguous low probability of meeting all requirements.

```{r load}
suppressMessages({library(survival); library(dplyr)})
library(bayesval)
YEAR <- 365.25
```

## Prepare data and split by recruiting centre

`status` is coded 1 = censored, 2 = dead, changed here to the framework's 0 and 1. There was too much missing data on meal calories, so it has been dropped; this is where the framework's multiple imputation options would apply. Retained covariates are analysed complete-case.

```{r data}
lung_cc <- lung |>
  transmute(inst,
            time   = time / YEAR,               # days -> years
            status = status - 1L,               # 1/2 -> 0/1
            age,
            sex    = factor(sex, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("male", "female")),
            ph.ecog, ph.karno, wt.loss) |>
  na.omit()

## Centre split: the three largest institutes develop, the rest validate.
inst_by_size <- as.integer(names(sort(table(lung_cc$inst), decreasing = TRUE)))
dev_inst <- inst_by_size[1:3]
train <- lung_cc |> filter(inst %in% dev_inst)  |> select(-inst)
test  <- lung_cc |> filter(!inst %in% dev_inst) |> select(-inst)

cat(sprintf("Train (institutes %s): n = %d, %d events\n",
            paste(sort(dev_inst), collapse = ", "),
            nrow(train), sum(train$status)))
cat(sprintf("Test  (other institutes): n = %d, %d events, %.0f%% censored\n",
            nrow(test), sum(test$status), 100 * mean(test$status == 0)))

fit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + ph.ecog + ph.karno + wt.loss,
             data = train, x = TRUE, y = TRUE)
```

## Posterior survival object and the deployment gate

The fitted model is carried onto the validation cohort as a posterior object giving survival probabilities. The gate, fixed before the read-out, requires simultaneously: Harrell C at least 0.65, slope in [0.80, 1.25] and positive net benefit at a 20% risk threshold. Headline horizon 1 year.

```{r gate}
ps <- psurv_external(fit, test, time = "time", status = "status",
                     horizons = c(1, 2), S = 500L, seed = 1)

hH <- 1L; tau <- 2; PT <- 0.20
C_MIN <- 0.65; SLOPE_LO <- 0.80; SLOPE_HI <- 1.25; NB_TOL <- 1e-8

metric_dnb <- function(pt, h) function(draw, w) {
  nb <- net_benefit_draw(draw, thresholds = pt, horizon = h, w = w)
  c(NB_model = nb$model, dNB = nb$model - max(nb$all, 0))
}
# Grouped Kaplan-Meier calibration: the cohort's short survival packs 1-year
# risks into the upper range, where the adaptive-hazard smoother is unstable, so
# the grouped estimator is the documented fallback here.
suite <- list(
  harrell = metric_harrell_c,
  uno     = function(d, w) metric_uno_c(d, w, tau = tau),
  gonen   = metric_gonen_k,
  citl    = function(d, w) metric_citl(d, w)[paste0("CITL_t", hH)],
  slope   = metric_cal_slope,
  ici     = function(d, w) metric_ici(d, w, horizon = hH, method = "group"),
  brier   = function(d, w) metric_brier(d, w)[c(paste0("Brier_t", hH), "IBS")],
  ipa     = function(d, w) metric_ipa(d, w)[paste0("IPA_t", hH)],
  r2d     = metric_r2d,
  nb      = metric_dnb(PT, hH))
```

## Bayesian read-out: posteriors and frequentist comparators

Summary statistics over all posterior draws, with the Bayesian bootstrap added, are set beside the usual frequentist point estimate and confidence interval.

```{r bayes}
post_bb <- propagate_many(ps, suite, weights = "bootstrap", seed = 1)

relabel <- function(m) {
  m <- sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", m)
  m <- sub("_t1\\b", "@1y", m); m <- sub("_t2\\b", "@2y", m); m
}
tab_bb <- posterior_table(post_bb) |> dplyr::mutate(metric = relabel(metric))

## Frequentist comparators on the mean linear predictor.
lp  <- colMeans(ps$eta)
dfv <- tibble::tibble(time = test$time, status = test$status)
freq_wald <- function(est, se) c(estimate = est, lower = est - 1.96 * se,
                                 upper = est + 1.96 * se)
ch <- concordance(Surv(time, status) ~ lp, data = dfv)
cu <- concordance(Surv(time, status) ~ lp, data = dfv, timewt = "n/G2", ymax = tau)
fr_harrell <- freq_wald(1 - ch$concordance, sqrt(ch$var))
fr_uno     <- freq_wald(1 - cu$concordance, sqrt(cu$var))
cs <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ lp, data = dfv)
fr_slope <- freq_wald(unname(coef(cs)), sqrt(vcov(cs)[1, 1]))

mean_draw <- list(surv2d = matrix(colMeans(ps$surv), nrow = ps$n), eta = lp,
                  time = test$time, status = test$status,
                  horizons = ps$horizons, n = ps$n, H = length(ps$horizons))
boot_ci <- function(metric_fn, B = 500L, seed = 7) {
  set.seed(seed); n <- ps$n
  v <- replicate(B, {
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    db <- list(surv2d = mean_draw$surv2d[idx, , drop = FALSE], eta = lp[idx],
               time = test$time[idx], status = test$status[idx],
               horizons = ps$horizons, n = n, H = length(ps$horizons))
    as.numeric(metric_fn(db, rep(1 / n, n))[1])
  })
  c(estimate = as.numeric(metric_fn(mean_draw, rep(1 / n, n))[1]),
    stats::quantile(v, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE))
}
fr_ibs <- boot_ci(function(d, w) metric_brier(d, w)["IBS"])
fr_ici <- boot_ci(function(d, w) metric_ici(d, w, horizon = hH, method = "group")["ICI"])
names(fr_ibs) <- names(fr_uno); names(fr_ici) <- names(fr_uno)

freq <- tibble::tibble(
  metric   = c("C_harrell", "C_uno", "cal_slope", "IBS", "ICI"),
  estimate = c(fr_harrell[1], fr_uno[1], fr_slope[1], fr_ibs[1], fr_ici[1]),
  lower    = c(fr_harrell[2], fr_uno[2], fr_slope[2], fr_ibs[2], fr_ici[2]),
  upper    = c(fr_harrell[3], fr_uno[3], fr_slope[3], fr_ibs[3], fr_ici[3]))

knitr::kable(posterior_vs_frequentist(tab_bb, freq),
             caption = "Bayesian posterior median [95% CrI] vs frequentist [95% CI]")
```

The posterior ICI is considerably higher than the frequentist point estimate, based on the posterior-mean prediction. Given only tens of training events, each individual draw is miscalibrated; that wide, high calibration posterior is the small-cohort signal.

## Deployment-gate probabilities

```{r gate-prob}
Jm <- unclass(post_bb); colnames(Jm) <- sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", colnames(Jm))
P_disc <- mean(Jm[, "C_harrell"] >= C_MIN)
P_cal  <- mean(Jm[, "cal_slope"] >= SLOPE_LO & Jm[, "cal_slope"] <= SLOPE_HI)
P_bene <- mean(Jm[, "dNB"] >  NB_TOL)
P_harm <- mean(Jm[, "dNB"] < -NB_TOL)
P_gate <- mean(Jm[, "C_harrell"] >= C_MIN &
               Jm[, "cal_slope"] >= SLOPE_LO & Jm[, "cal_slope"] <= SLOPE_HI &
               Jm[, "dNB"] > NB_TOL)
cat(sprintf("P(discrimination adequate) = %.2f\n", P_disc))
cat(sprintf("P(calibration acceptable)  = %.2f\n", P_cal))
cat(sprintf("P(net clinical benefit)    = %.2f\n", P_bene))
cat(sprintf("P(net harm)                = %.2f\n", P_harm))
cat(sprintf("P(JOINT deployment gate)   = %.2f  (naive product %.2f)\n",
            P_gate, P_disc * P_cal * P_bene))
```

## Posterior decision curve and calibration check

```{r curves, fig.width=5, fig.height=4.4}
pnb <- posterior_net_benefit(ps, thresholds = seq(0.1, 0.7, 0.05),
                             horizon = hH, weights = "bootstrap",
                             draws = 300L, seed = 4)
plot_net_benefit(pnb)

ppc <- tryCatch(
  ppc_calibration(ps, horizon = hH, method = "group", draws = 200L, seed = 3),
  error = function(e) NULL)
if (!is.null(ppc)) plot_calibration_band(ppc)
```

Hence overall probability of deployment is very small, in contrast to the fairly non-dramatic conclusion from considering discrimination alone. The poor calibration is reflected in the low overall probability of deployment returned when considering the joint distribution.
